title: The Cycle of History
subtitle: By the time people realize its true nature, it has already moved.

trails.title: Applying Chladni Plate Sound Propagation
trails.description: A metal plate, a grain of sand, an element of sound. Simple and effective.

content.text:
Required Materials:

A square sheet of metal 

Other shapes and materials can also be used, observing the differences they produce is equally entertaining.

Sand

Flour, salt, or sugar can also be used, but be careful, they're not easy to clean once they get into those body crevices.

An element of sound

Yes, that's me, glad to help. You can also find any friend who knows how to sing and make vibrations, or say, dance.

Working Principles:

It is known that sound is produced by vibration and propagates in the form of waves, and different sounds have different frequencies of vibration, so certain sounds can produce fixed waves under certain conditions, thereby representing certain patterns.

Operating Steps:

First, place the square metal sheet, hereinafter referred to as the plate, on a stable and well-fixed smooth solid surface.

This is to prevent phenomena such as slipping, an important step.

Second, the sound element is made to contact the plate and emit sound at a specific frequency.

The Scientific Computing Center has compiled the wavebands corresponding to the 26 letter shapes—you can ask Mr. Ulrich for a copy, he is a very generous gentleman.

Third, observe the pattern and draw conclusions.

Wasn't that simple? You can do it alone at home—try it and see what pattern your favorite music program turns into.

items.text: The Cycle of History
The Hall of Apeiron
Heed my words, 37.
That scroll is a sacred relic passed down from the wise sages of Apeiron, safeguarded by the 6s and entrusted only to believers who brave Apeiron's test.
It has the power of harmonization and reconciliation. You may keep it until you've fully grasped the secrets shared with you by Apeiron.
But you will not share it with some organization affiliated with humans, and certainly do not allow them to study it.
The inevitable disagreement is finally upon them.
888 grabs 37 by the arm and drags her out of the lab.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Sharing the scroll is sharing wisdom and knowledge with others, like what we have done through our doctrinal meetings and receiving visitors from the outside world. It is for the sake of spreading the light of Truth, is it not?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The human researchers, they have also discovered many brilliant theorems.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Before the "Emanation" cut us off, we had these types of communications with the outside world. It was fun, unlike what came after.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I'm sure by sharing this scroll, the code from Apeiron will be deciphered.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I must prove that the light of Truth still glimmers!
She stands her ground.
She is right. With their faith shattered, people need something new to keep them going.
And this time, her suggestion makes sense in a practical way—a quality often missing from her previous ideas.
With the island no longer shielding them, the school must find another way to survive the "Emanation." In their moment of weakness, they need a powerful ally more than ever.
But how can you be sure the scroll will only be used for researching the ritual?
How can you ensure that the humans won't exploit it to create weapons of destruction?
The Custodian looks up at the fractured dome.
The speckled daylight illuminates her cool complexion.
Before joining the School of Apeiron, my people and I had wandered the world for ages. Our long lives made it difficult for us to truly fit in with the world.
Daughter of Truth, I implore you to hear the words of this old soul.
Humans have indeed achieved incredible feats, and their enlightenment has even touched my soul.
But unfortunately, most humans do not have an inherent respect for knowledge or its boundaries. They only chase after power blindly.
I have experienced it firsthand. I tried to guide and persuade them, but ultimately, I failed. That is why I am here now.
What you're deciding to share is not only knowledge, but it is a ritual, a piece of power.
A ritual designed for harmonization, created for the devout believers, and created for the sages seeking the Truth.
Yet, on the other hand, it can also be used for unspeakable horrors, such as silencers on guns, suppressors on rifles, or even on nuclear bombs.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It won't!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 888, I won't let this happen. I promise.
You can't promise anything, Ms. Vertin. You are too young.
Too inexperienced to comprehend the dark nature of history.
A valid and powerful observation.
The hall itself, ravaged by war, now stands as a testament to the banshee's claim.
Even 37 is speechless.
But it's the Truth we're talking about. What could possibly outweigh the Truth?
An unexpected voice speaks up.
To everyone's surprise, the rhetorician does not raise any objections this time.
If all it takes is lending someone a scroll to unlock unspeakable secrets, why not do it?
Haven't the failures of the past four years proven that a stagnant mindset does not bring forth the light of Truth?
As individuals devoted to critical thinking, should the pursuit of Truth not be our primary goal in life?
My brothers and sisters, do not let hatred stop you, and don't let the dust of the phenomenal world blind you.
He waves his hand and gets up from his seat.
And remember, it was 37 who passed the test and earned the scroll. It is her rightful responsibility to handle this situation.
He looks elsewhere, his demeanor suggesting a lack of interest rather than genuine support for the argument.
Otherwise, what other choice do we have?
He shrugs and walks out of the hall.
Behind him, the Star of Hermes clenches her fist with resolve.
To the murmuring, doubting crowd, she speaks again, loud and clear.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I have made up my mind.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I will share this scroll with Laplace. We will decipher the code together.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The Truth is the Truth. It should not be swayed by anything else.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Please, everyone, cast your pebble if you agree with me! If 6 were here, he too would have called for a vote.
Some of them decide to leave the hall instead, but most stay and use the pebbles in their hands to speak for them.
Her victory arrives with a gentle sigh from the corner.
*sigh*
War and smoke have long left this place.
An area has been cleared for takeoff.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Lilya, are you certain about this?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Absolutely. See the nice weather today? Much better than the day we landed.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: No wind, no cloud, the clear sky, and that giant moon!
Sitting tight on her Su-01ве, she gives a quick pat to the scroll secured on her belt.
This is the essence of Apeiron's goodwill, in their newfound alliance with Laplace.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Can't find a better day to deliver the package. It's just to the headquarters, not even going outside of Europe. Three hours is more than enough.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'm done being stuck on this suffocating island. Nobody can stop me from taking this flight!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The headquarters are at least 768 nautical miles away, and you have no protection during the long flight. It's dangerous!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And we have only seven hours until the "Storm."

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Dangerous? Maybe. But this is an exhilarating flight in the "Storm," Sonetto! What better chance than now to push Zeno into updating their Flying Manual?
She takes a few long gulps from her canteen and warms up her broomstick, brimming with anticipation as if she were going to a carnival.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Besides, what's wrong with a bit of oil painting on me? Should be a nice badge of honor.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Mate, that's quite a distance. Just be sure not to go toppling into the Mediterranean Sea!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Heheheh, Red 38 is no way an APPLe II!
She soars higher and higher until Regulus shrinks to a tiny red dot on the beach.
From the corner of her eye, she notices shadows slowly creeping toward her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Uh-oh, Manus Olitiaus? We didn't kill them all off?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I don't have time for you, little stingray rats.
The Olitiaus trail close behind her.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Still got your speed, huh? I guess the death of your boss didn't faze you much.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh?
A swollen blimp comes into view, filled with a dark substance and throbbing like a beating heart.
The creature's soft, tentacle-like turrets slowly rise and lock onto Lilya.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A Manus aircraft? Worth a fight.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Haha, bring it on! Your downfall will be an explosive orchestra over the waters!
To safely cast the immunity ritual, two conditions must be met.
(1) have the power to wield it

items.speaker: X
items.text: Yes, Ms. Titor has derived the formula, and my team has finished designing the prototype converter.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Now, we just need the bigwigs "upstairs" to approve the experiment application.

items.speaker: X
items.text: This is an unprecedented chance to rob the "Storm" of its energy. I wouldn't miss this for anything.
(2) minimize the side effects

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The scroll of Apeiron has shown great potential in protecting casters from the ritual. It is expected to outperform the Coleman protection rituals.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The sheer variety of side effects is concerning, but we already have a list of 122 curses and their effects. Once the scroll arrives, we will test and record its reactions to each of the effects.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This should speed up our analysis considerably.
But this isn't enough.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: How can we get humans to make use of this ritual?
He stands up and paces around the cluttered room.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ideally, the incantation is made into a tool like the Manus mask, or Laplace's incantation soft disk.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: However, this would require a thorough analysis and mastery of the ritual! Manus Vindictae could create the mask because Arcana is just that excellent of a caster.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But we don't have that kind of excellence or the time. That's why I came up with a clever alternative—to let everyone be a caster instead.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The problem is, humans can't cast at all to begin with! Ugh!
Logic is failing to produce the desired breakthroughs. Enigma sits back down at the table, holding his head in despair.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is there nothing else we can do?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: So, this is the plan of the imaginary numbers.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You want to use the "waves of pneuma" and the reconciliation of the scroll to allow everyone to recite the "Storm" immunity ritual?
37 ponders with great interest, as if it were just another game.
The collaboration with Laplace is going well—they have just shared all their information on the subject.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. What do you think, 37?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: An ugly plan it is!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: There is no grace or beauty in this approach. It is purely driven by practicality and uses clever tactics to make things fit. How typical of imaginary numbers.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What? Hah! It sounds pretty cool to me!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Taking advantage of the "Storm," it's about time we plundered it instead, haha!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm, it really looks like we should throw this plan into the sea.
37 insists, subtly shifting her seat away from Regulus.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You're not trying to comprehend the ritual, Vertin, but scrambling to make use of it before the "Emanation" arrives.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Isn't making use of it enough for our purposes?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No! The theory is incomplete. You will be hindered by impossible obstacles in no time.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Mister, could you show me the incantation? I want to see it, too.
She glances at the device, hoping for an answer. But the other end of the call has been silent for a while.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Laplace is looking for a safe method to deliver the incantation. Given the incidents before, some time is required for the application procedure.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Once received, please do not read it out by any means. The side effects are extremely deadly.
The chief assistant explains to her reassuringly.
Finally, someone speaks again.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Apologies. We took some time to test the delivery methods.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: For your safety, only the text of the incantation will be delivered. The exact pronunciation will be sent to the Timekeeper later.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah, thanks, mate.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Since the island has no visual communication, we will send the incantation letter by letter through a Chladni Plate, a technique that converts simple patterns to sound waves.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Ahh, enough with the mumbo jumbo! There's no time for details.
Annoyed, he interrupts his rambling and gets straight to the point.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Anyway, Timekeeper, we'll need the help of that lady—Ms. Radio, right?

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Huh?!
Flattered, the blue flower on Ms. Radio perks up.
No ordinary signal could reach this island. Since their arrival, she's been diligently managing their communications.
As a result, she was somewhat reduced to being just a radio.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Yes, somebody, please find her a metal square plate, fix it on a sturdy base, and pour sand on it.
Sonetto and Regulus get to work immediately.
Fortunately, there's no shortage of metals and sand on the island. A makeshift receiving station is quickly built.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Now, a special recording will be sent to you. Please stay by the edge of the plate, embrace the sound and, um, uh, groove along.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: I assume you mean "vibrate"?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: No no no no no, that's just rude ... but uh, yes, exactly.
He stammers.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: If all goes well, the vibrations will move the sand and visualize the text in a pattern.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: We have 12 recordings ready, each representing a letter in the incantation. We'll play the first one when you're ready.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: O-of course, my pleasure!
She trembles with excitement, ready to give her all for this important task.
As she grooves with the signal, a pattern begins to form on the plate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: First one's done, Mr. Ulrich.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Alright, 11 to go.
The transmission continues as planned, each letter falling into place like pieces of a puzzle.
Until finally, the last letter is recorded on the page.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This incantation ...
The sight is hard to believe.
How can this be?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: W-what? Are you reading it in your head?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah! Don't tell me even thinking about it can trigger the curse!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, it's just ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I can read this language.
La unua cirklo.
The language is not unfamiliar. The incantation for unlocking the suitcase is inscribed in the same tongue.
The questions are, who taught this, and when?
Was it on the eve of the new millennium, when everything was a blank?
Was it ... Mother?
A myriad of thoughts flood the mind.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 37, I think I know what it says.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It means "the first circle."
TO BE CONTINUED…
